summary: Added the Ollama extension foundation: a typed REST client, a small long-running-job registry with cancellation, and a host-lifecycle module that detects the binary, checks versions, and drives install/update per platform (Windows silent Inno Setup, macOS .app expansion, Linux user-owned tarball + managed serve). Shared types, a model-listing service that enriches /api/tags with /api/show at bounded concurrency, and tests were added, and the work was committed as checkpoint 1.
decisions: Job registry enforces one active job per kind; the last finished job stays visible until the next one starts so the UI can render its outcome.
Job lifecycle exposes stage and percent plus start/finish timestamps, with cancellation via AbortController and a JobActiveError on duplicate starts.

On Linux, the extension manages its own copy under ~/.local/share/ollama-gizmo (user-owned tarball) and writes a pid file for stop; managed-update is indicated via a HostStatus note when the resolved binary isn't already the managed copy.

startDetachedServe is async, opens the log file once via fsPromises.open, and reuses the fd for both stdout and stderr to avoid leaking open handles; pid is captured and written to the pid file in the linux flow (no pgrep recovery).

Shared types (JobKind/JobStatus/JobSnapshot and Ollama-related shapes) live in shared/types.ts and are imported into server/jobs.ts which re-exports them, so the web bundle can use them without importing server code.
Model listing lives in shared/models.ts so both the server extension's models.list operation and the Pi provider's refreshModels can use the same tags + bounded-concurrency show enrichment.
errors: jobs.test.ts 'tracks a job through success' failed because the run callback referenced the still-undefined `snapshot` returned by registry.start synchronously inside the callback, throwing and failing the job. Fixed by dropping that assertion and only asserting signal.aborted inside the callback.

host.test.ts 'includes the managed Linux install' failed on Windows because the expectation used a literal '/bin/ollama' suffix while host.ts joins via path.sep. Fixed by using node:path join in the expectation.
